title: Cringebot3000 helps you post AI slop to LinkedIn. Sadly, it worked.
excerpt: Turns out a deliberately cringy AI slop generator is better at LinkedIn than I am. This doesn't bode well.
content_html:
I stared deep into the heart of LinkedIn AI cringe slop. Darkness (and engagement) stared back.

By Katie Notopoulos

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Senior Correspondent covering technology and culture

They say to be cringe is to be free. And on LinkedIn, I needed a taste of freedom. Which is why I fully embraced using Cringebot 3000, a website that creates purposely grating AI-generated slop for you to post to LinkedIn.

Why on Earth would you want that? That's the wrong question. The better one is: How did we get to this point?

Cringebot 3000 is the unholy creation of Peter Epstein, who runs a Los Angeles-based PR firm for advertising industry clients. After the website blew up on Reddit and the influential Hacker News site this week, I caught up with him over the phone to find out what kind of twisted mind would aspire to be the Oppenheimer of LinkedIn slop.

"The goal is to make it a little less serious and try to take what's become its own sort of form, like poetry — LinkedIn 'thought leadership' is its own form — and try to take that form and make it a little more fun and a little more silly," he explained.

He wanted to try vibecoding something with Claude, and first created the site at the beginning of this year, but only more recently fine-tuned it to be reliable at mass-producing this kind of slop at scale.

LinkedIn has an AI slop problem and I'm not helping

LinkedIn has long had a problem with cheesiness and people posting purposely engagement-baiting posts. It's been almost a decade since we witnessed the terrifying birth of a new posting form known as "broetry" — posts where:

They use line breaks for every sentence.
And the content is something like
What potty training my toddler taught me about 2b2 SaaS sales.

The ability to use AI to write this kind of stuff has turned LinkedIn into a real slophouse. LinkedIn is well aware and trying to fight it: it recently added a feature where you can report a post for "AI slop" the same way you might for harassment or spam.

"People complain about LinkedIn AI slop, but was LinkedIn that great before AI slop?" Epstein pointed out.

Partly because of this kind of content, I haven't found LinkedIn to be a "fun" place to post. But the tantalizing idea of becoming a LinkedInfluencer now dangled before me, warm and weightless. I needed to shake the shackles of caring about "good" posts or "seeming human" and plunge into the deep end of the slop pool.

Now sure, I could use any LLM to come up with some quasi-inspirational business wisdom pablum to post on LinkedIn. But Cringebot 3000 makes it even easier. Just type in a topic — could be a single word, and then select from eight separate flavors, such as "The Vulnerability Post (oversharing with a motivational twist)", "The Inspiring Story (finding life lessons everywhere)"or "The Corporate Dropout (quit the 9-5 to follow my passion)".

I typed in "AI in journalism" as my topic and chose "You Go Girl! (empowerment culture and smashing glass ceilings)" for the style.

The output was perfect LinkedIn slop: a meandering story with a grippy opening sentence and a corny kernel of truth at the end. It was loaded with hashtags (and a disclaimer at the very bottom that it was written by Cringebot 3000).

Here's the text (you can skim it):

Okay so I need to tell you all something that happened to me last Tuesday that I am still not fully recovered from.

I was pitching a story to my editor about AI writing tools replacing journalists, and I accidentally sent the draft that my AI assistant had written ABOUT ME to the entire newsroom listserv.

The AI had described me as "a mid-level content facilitator with moderate narrative instincts."

Moderate. Narrative. Instincts.

I cried in the bathroom for eleven minutes.

But here is what happened next, and this is the part that matters.

Every woman in that newsroom replied-all within twenty minutes. Not to laugh. To share their own AI horror stories. The investigative reporter whose AI fact-checker confidently cited a country that no longer exists. The foreign correspondent whose translation bot rendered her entire interview in the subjunctive mood. The editor whose AI headline generator called a piece about the Supreme Court "a fun romp."

We built something that afternoon in that reply-all thread that no algorithm could have generated.

We built a coalition of women who refuse to let machines define our narrative instincts, moderate or otherwise.

The AI didn't replace us. It accidentally introduced us to each other.

Now we have a weekly meeting. We are rewriting the rules of how women in journalism engage with these tools, on our terms, with our voices, telling our stories.

The AI called me moderate.

The sisterhood said: absolutely not.

#WomenInJournalism #AIInJournalism #MediaInnovation #WomenSupportingWomen #JournalismTwitter #TechAndMedia #GlassCeilingSmashed #SisterhoodIsPowerful #OwnYourNarrative #cringebot3000

This post was generated with tongue firmly in cheek by LinkedIn CringeBot 3000. (link in comments)

Awful, right? I immediately copy and pasted it to my LinkedIn and let that sweet, sweet engagement roll in.

The reaction was mixed. People who knew me well recognized it was an AI-generated joke.

But according to LinkedIn's analytics of the reach of my post, 96% of viewers were people not in my network — strangers who didn't know this is would be highly out of character for me to write. I started seeing some comments from strangers as if this was a genuine anecdote about the workplace.

Oh no, what have I done

"I love this so much! Way to hold each other up and take control of the literal narrative!" commented someone I didn't know.

To make things worse, the post itself was a rousing success by LinkedIn standards. I got far more engagement and comments on this than I have for any of my other recent posts with links to articles I wrote or other career news.

Basically, the Cringebot3000 is way better at LinkedIn than I am.

Like a true LinkedIn Thought Leader, I am choosing to learn from my failures. Whatever shriveled shred of humanity that still flickers inside me that normally prevents me from posting garbage on LinkedIn is something I should treasure, not be ashamed of. No more AI slop for me. Well, unless Cringebot4000 comes out.

content_html_zh:
我深入研究了 LinkedIn 人工智能令人畏惧的本质。 达克妮丝（和订婚）也回以凝视。

作者：Katie Notopoulos 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 资深记者报道科技与文化

他们说，畏缩就是自由。 在 LinkedIn 上，我需要尝尝自由的滋味。 这就是为什么我完全喜欢使用 Cringebot 3000，这是一个网站，专门创建人工智能生成的令人厌烦的废话，供你发布到 LinkedIn。

你到底为什么想要那个？ 这是错误的问题。 更好的是：我们是如何走到这一步的？

Cringebot 3000 是彼得·爱泼斯坦 (Peter Epstein) 的邪恶创造，他在洛杉矶经营着一家为广告行业客户服务的公关公司。 本周，该网站在 Reddit 和颇具影响力的黑客新闻网站上炸毁后，我通过电话联系了他，想了解什么样的扭曲思想会渴望成为 LinkedIn 的奥本海默。

“我们的目标是让它不那么严肃，并尝试采取自己的形式，比如诗歌——LinkedIn的‘思想领导力’就是它自己的形式——并尝试采用这种形式，让它变得更有趣、更愚蠢，”他解释道。

他想尝试与克劳德一起进行振动编码，并在今年年初首次创建了该网站，但直到最近才对它进行了微调，使其能够可靠地大规模生产这种斜坡。

LinkedIn 遇到 AI 问题，但我没有提供帮助

LinkedIn 长期以来一直存在着俗气和人们故意发布吸引参与的帖子的问题。 自从我们见证了一种名为“broetry”的新发帖形式的可怕诞生以来，已经过去近十年了——发帖的位置：

他们在每个句子中都使用换行符。内容类似于我的孩子的如厕训练教我有关 2b2 SaaS 销售的内容。

使用人工智能编写此类内容的能力已经将 LinkedIn 变成了一个真正的破烂屋。 LinkedIn 很清楚并试图与之抗争：它最近添加了一项功能，您可以举报“AI slop”帖子，就像举报骚扰或垃圾邮件一样。

“人们抱怨 LinkedIn 的人工智能技术落后，但在人工智能技术落后之前，LinkedIn 真的那么好吗？” 爱泼斯坦指出。

部分原因是此类内容，我不认为 LinkedIn 是一个“有趣”的发帖场所。 但成为 LinkedIn 网红的诱人想法现在就在我面前晃来晃去，温暖而轻盈。 我需要摆脱关心“好”帖子或“看起来像人”的束缚，跳入污水池的深处。

现在可以肯定的是，我可以利用任何法学硕士来想出一些准鼓舞人心的商业智慧宝典，然后发布在 LinkedIn 上。 但 Cringebot 3000 使这一切变得更加容易。 只需输入一个主题 - 可以是一个单词，然后从八种不同的风格中进行选择，例如“漏洞帖子（带有激励性扭曲的过度分享）”，“鼓舞人心的故事（到处寻找人生教训）”或“公司辍学者（退出朝九晚五，追随我的激情）”。

我输入“新闻业中的人工智能”作为我的主题，并选择“You Go Girl！ （赋权文化和粉碎玻璃天花板）”的风格。

输出结果是完美的 LinkedIn 语言：一个曲折的故事，开头句引人入胜，结尾是老生常谈的真相。 它加载了主题标签（并且在最底部有一个免责声明，表明它是由 Cringebot 3000 编写的）。

正文如下（大家可以浏览一下）：

好吧，我需要告诉你们上周二发生在我身上的事情，我还没有完全恢复过来。我正在向我的编辑推销一篇关于人工智能写作工具取代记者的故事，我不小心将我的人工智能助理写的关于我的草稿发送到了整个新闻编辑室列表服务器。人工智能将我描述为“具有适度叙事本能的中级内容促进者。”中等。 叙述。 本能。我在浴室里哭了十一分钟。但这就是接下来发生的事情，这就是重要的部分。新闻编辑室里的每个女人都在二十分钟内回复了。 不许笑。 分享他们自己的人工智能恐怖故事。 调查记者的人工智能事实核查员自信地引用了一个不再存在的国家。 这位外国记者的翻译机器人以虚拟语气进行了整个采访。 编辑的人工智能标题生成器称一篇关于最高法院的文章是“有趣的闹剧”。那天下午，我们在那个回复所有线程中构建了任何算法都无法生成的东西。我们建立了一个女性联盟，拒绝让机器定义我们的叙事本能，无论是温和的还是其他的。人工智能并没有取代我们。 它无意中把我们介绍给了彼此。现在我们每周开一次会。 我们正在重写新闻业女性如何使用这些工具的规则，用我们的方式，用我们的声音，讲述我们的故事。人工智能称我为温和派。姐妹会说：绝对不是。#WomenInJournalism #AIInJournalism #MediaInnovation #WomenSupportingWomen #JournalismTwitter #TechAndMedia #GlassCeilingSmashed #SisterhoodIsPowerful #OwnYourNarrative #cringebot3000这篇文章是由 LinkedIn CringeBot 3000 开玩笑地生成的。 （链接在评论里）

太糟糕了，对吧？ 我立即将其复制并粘贴到我的 LinkedIn 上，让甜蜜的订婚随之而来。

反应是混合的。 熟悉我的人都知道这是人工智能生成的笑话。

但根据LinkedIn对我的帖子影响范围的分析，96%的观众不是我的网络中的人——不知道这一点的陌生人对于我的写作来说是非常不符合性格的。 我开始看到一些陌生人的评论，好像这是关于工作场所的真实轶事。

哦不，我做了什么

“我非常喜欢这个！ 互相扶持并控制文字叙述的方式！” 一个我不认识的人评论道。

更糟糕的是，按照 LinkedIn 的标准，这篇文章本身就取得了巨大的成功。 与我最近发表的任何其他带有我写的文章或其他职业新闻链接的帖子相比，我对此的参与和评论要多得多。

基本上，Cringebot3000 在 LinkedIn 上的表现比我好得多。

像真正的 LinkedIn 思想领袖一样，我选择从失败中学习。 无论我体内仍然闪烁着多少枯萎的人性，通常会阻止我在 LinkedIn 上发布垃圾内容，我都应该珍惜而不是感到羞耻。 我不再需要人工智能了。 好吧，除非 Cringebot4000 出来。
